messages_bodies:
Hi Sean,

Thanks for the call earlier — this was helpful. I have a couple of follow-ups from our security and engineering teams about exactly what Redwood stores when we send prompts and receive outputs. They need concise answers for procurement and for our risk committee: 

1) Are raw prompts persisted anywhere by default (plain text or as log entries)?
2) Are generated outputs treated differently from prompts in storage policy?
3) Where are these logs/resident copies stored (region / cloud / Redwood-managed)?
4) What are the default retention windows for prompts, outputs, and model logs?
5) Is there a way to opt out of prompt/output retention for our account or toggle it per-environment?

Appreciate a short summary we can include in the SOW.

Cheers,
Emily
Emily Ryan
Director, Platform Ops — BrightHealth Tech
emily.ryan@brighthealth.com
+1 (617) 555-0192

Hi Emily — thanks again for the time. Short answers here and attaching a one‑page summary for your security and procurement team (attached). More detail below. TL;DR: prompts are NOT stored as searchable plaintext by default for hosted accounts; we retain encrypted log artifacts for 30 days for operational debugging and 180 days for aggregated telemetry; enterprise/Private deployments can disable prompt logging entirely and pin residency.

Details:
- Default behavior (Hosted API):
  • Prompt text: persisted transiently in encrypted request logs for 30 days to support debugging and quality monitoring; not indexed for search.
  • Model outputs: stored as part of the same encrypted logs for 30 days by default; customers can request longer retention for audit purposes via contract.
  • System/model logs & traces: aggregated telemetry retained 180 days; token-level traces are redacted.
- Residency & encryption:
  • Hosted data is stored in customer-selected region (us/eu) where supported; encryption at rest with KMS; cross-region replication only for failover with customer consent.
  • Dedicated/Private: you can elect VPC/on-prem where telemetry and logs stay in your environment and Redwood control plane only stores metadata.
- Controls we offer:
  • Logging toggle (account-level): disable storing prompt/output payloads — useful for PHI/PII-sensitive workflows.
  • Retention adjustment: configurable via contract (e.g., 90/180/365 days).
  • Data residency lock: pin to US regions with documented SOC 2 controls.

Next steps I propose:
1) Technical call with Ben (security engineer) to walk through the Drive diagram and confirm encryption/KMS with your infra team.
2) We prepare a short addendum for the SOW specifying retention window and logging toggle.
3) If you want, we can spin a Private evaluation in your VPC for a short POC where prompt logging is disabled.

I'll drop the one-pager into Drive. Looping Marissa for procurement alignment.

—Sean
Sean Gallagher
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.com

Hi Emily — quick follow-up after internal sync with product: a couple clarifications on technical points you flagged.

1) "Prompt text persisted transiently" above means we write encrypted request payloads to an append-only log for operational visibility. Those files are encrypted with customer/Redwood-managed KMS keys depending on deployment. They are accessible to ops for incident response only with elevation and audit logs.
2) "Not indexed for search": we do not add prompt text to the search index used by our console; logs are queryable by date/job-id but prompt payloads are redacted in console UI unless your account enables unredacted debug mode.

Attached to this thread is the one‑page summary I mentioned. Ben can walk through it with your security team.

Best,
Sean
